Replay

Authoring captured floors

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Existing Replay savesAcceptance gates

Open cave.tscn and edit its floor1_def / floor2_def resources. The defaults live in levels/level_1.tres and level_2.tres; the original Cavecrawl project is separate. Each definition selects a floor PackedScene, chest stock, a wave plan and the rectangular rift used by the pure navigation model.

The loader validates both definitions before opening a Session. It instantiates each floor outside the SceneTree, reads its four direct Marker2D children ChestSpawn, DoorSpawn, Den1, Den2, and destroys the temporary instance. The scene must have a Node2D root with an identity transform. Marker positions are in simulation coordinates: x 0–640, y 0–370. The rift must be a nonempty rectangle inside those bounds. Its explicit rift_min / rift_max fields must describe the same obstacle as the art; this loader does not convert Godot navigation meshes.

gems and torches accept 0–99. A zero stock leaves an empty chest slot; player inventory retains its normal per-item limits. wave_counts and wave_rests must have equal lengths between one and eight. Counts accept 0–255; rests accept 0–65535 simulation ticks at 20 Hz. The 16-dweller pool bounds simultaneous live mobs; larger waves spawn as slots become available. A zero-count wave is legal.

The resulting two Floor values are copied into World. The host's values travel with snapshots, replay history, save files and approved migration checkpoints. Clients may have different local definition values: gameplay and entity positions use the received world. Changes to the original Resource after initialization do not alter an active game. Start a new game to use a changed definition, or implement an explicit recorded rule change if live editing is required.

PackedScenes remain local presentation assets, retained independently of the resource slots. Their contents are not serialized. Changing local art or navigation assets can therefore change appearance without changing a saved world's gameplay values; distribute matching assets when visual agreement matters. Mutating the retained PackedScene itself is not supported as a live authoring operation.

Decoration is generated from the saved world seed and floor depth using the original splitmix32 recipe. Each nonzero seed produces ten alternating rocks and mushrooms at integer positions. Seed zero disables scatter. The default seed 1337 has checksums 976669602 and 4288723372 for the two floors. Decorations are views; they do not consume gameplay RNG or enter collision state.

Existing Replay saves#

Cavecrawl content is now 0x4341564552504c39. C4 corrected wave pacing and den selection; C5 preserves avatar state on descent and separates run reset rules. C6 retains the relic across descent and releases it in place on restart. C7 retains relic ownership through death, respawn and ordinary disconnect. C8 records the observed authority and adopts the previous host’s relic on takeover. The ordinary loader rejects prior C1–C8 content, even where the value layout is unchanged. Gameplay protocol 7 and checkpoint format 4 are unchanged. This is an explicit conversion of earlier Replay saves, not an importer for original Kit saves.

Build the converter and give it an existing source and a new destination:

Shell
nix develop --command odin build examples/replay_cavecrawl/tools/upgrade_save \
  -collection:godot=. -out:/tmp/replay-cave-upgrade
/tmp/replay-cave-upgrade /path/to/old.replay /path/to/converted.replay

The converter validates the old archive, copies its complete world and session ledgers, maps pending actions into the new command shape, and adds an already-playing lobby with default seat names. Content 1 receives the original default floors; content 2 retains its captured floors. The first connected seat becomes party leader. It then computes the new schema contract and hashes. It preserves the source and refuses to replace an existing file or symlink. Publication requires same-directory hard-link support. Conversion alone grants no authority and does not increment the epoch; normal resume or Room recovery still applies its authority rules. Use the owning profile/token when resuming and retain the original archive. Protocol-7/content-1 through content-8 saves are supported by this converter. C3 conversion preserves the complete checkpoint and its scheduled spawn/rest deadlines; later spawns use corrected pacing. C4/C5/C6/C7 conversion also preserves all saved values; future transitions use current rules. Lobby metadata/commands motivated content 3; gameplay protocol 7 and checkpoint layout 4 remain unchanged.

Acceptance gates#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/definitions_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/definitions_network_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_cave/upgrade/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_cave/scatter_run.sh

These check captured Resource/marker edits and fresh-process resume, host settings received by default-resource clients/observers under simulated network faults, invalid definitions, a genuine old-binary save converted and resumed, and original versus native/WASM scatter coordinates. The broader campaign and migration gates exercise the same expanded world schema.

C8 adds authority_known and authority_seat to World. Old-world descriptors keep the frozen C3–C7 layout. Conversion preserves prior fields and seeds the new observation from the validated checkpoint header’s local_seat, independently of lobby leadership. Adoption occurs on the first resumed simulation tick.

C9 adds generation-bound dweller Hit occurrences without changing saved world layout. C8 conversion preserves its authority observation exactly. Both native converters refuse coordinated archives; see impact compatibility.
